source.note: Full text of ASME BPVC Section II, Part B (Nonferrous Material Specifications) — SB-511 - Specification for Nickel-Iron-Chromium-Silicon Alloy Bars and Shapes — as supplied by Daniel Velasquez on 2026-09-07 and extracted from the supplied PDF with marker-pdf. `data` is the extractor's output verbatim — the drop's own `document`, `part`, `figures` and `pages` blocks, with the page-by-page block tree, its HTML, tables and layout coordinates unedited. This file IS the source document, so `transcribed_from` names its own path: it is the artefact under review, not a transcription of one. The volume was supplied as one combined PDF and cut into parts at its own headings, so this file is a page-range slice of a single extraction and its page ids (PDF pages None–None, no printed page numbers on these pages) are the combined document's own, not renumbered from 0. Front matter (cover and title page, contents, list of sections, foreword, statement of policy, personnel, correspondence, summary of changes, cross-referencing) and back matter (back cover) were deleted from the drop before supply and are NOT filed; the drop's `content.json`, `index.json`, `meta.json` and `README.md` are retained beside the kind folders, unfiled, for the same reason. The edition — 2025 Edition (ASME BPVC.II.B-2025), issued 2025-07-01 — is stated on the title page, which this drop no longer carries as a filed cut: it survives only inside the retained `content.json`, so no filed cut of this standard prints its own edition. This cut carries no figure.

(Identical with ASTM Specification B511-01(2009) except that certification has been made mandatory.)
SPECIFICATION FOR NICKEL-IRON-CHROMIUM-SILICON ALLOY BARS AND SHAPES
[Identical with ASTM Specification B 511-01(2009) except that certification has been made mandatory.]

1.1 This specification covers wrought alloys UNS N08330 and UNS N08332 in the form of hot-finished and cold-finished bar and shapes intended for heat-resisting applications and general corrosive service.
1.2 The values stated in inch-pound units are to be regarded as the standard. The values given in parentheses are for information only.

1.3 This standard does not purport to address all of the safety concerns, if any, associated with its use. It is the responsibility of the user of this standard to become familiar with all hazards including those identified in the appropriate Material Safety Data Sheet (MSDS) for this product/material as provided by the manufacturer, to establish appropriate safety and health practices, and determine the applicability of regulatory limitations prior to use.

3.1 Definitions of Terms Specific to This Standard:
3.1.1 bar, n — material round, rectangular, hexagonal, octagonal, or square solid section, furnished in straight lengths.
3.1.2 shapes, n — material of solid section in such forms as angles, channels, tees, I-beams, and four-fluted bars.

4.1 It is the responsibility of the purchaser to specify all requirements that are necessary for the safe and satisfactory performance of material ordered under this specification. Examples of such requirements include, but are not limited to the following:
4.1.1 Alloy (Table 1), 4.1.2 Quantity (weight or number of pieces), 4.1.3 ASTM designation and year of issue, 4.1.4 Section (round, square, I-beam, etc.), 4.1.5 Dimension, including length,
A Applies to round bar only. For other cross-sections and shapes the minimum elongation shall be 25%.
B Element shall be determined arithmetically by difference.
4.1.7 Samples for Product (Check) Analysis — State whether samples for product (check) analysis shall be furnished.

4.1.8 Purchaser Inspection — If a purchaser wishes to witness tests or inspections of material at the place of manufacture, the purchase order must so state indicating which tests or inspections are to be witnessed.
5.1 All material shall be furnished in the heat-treated condition, except that cold-drawn hexagons may be given a cold-draw sizing pass subsequent to the final heat treatment.
NOTE 1 — Hot-finished rectangular bar in widths 10 in. (254 mm) and under may be furnished as hot-finished plate with sheared or cut edges in accordance with Specification B 536.
6.1 The material shall conform to the requirements as to chemical composition specified in Table 2.
6.2 If a product (check) analysis is performed by the purchaser, the material shall conform to the product (check) analysis variations in accordance with Specification B 880.
7.1 The mechanical properties of the material at room temperature shall conform to those shown in Table 1.
7.2 Grain Size — Annealed alloy UNS N08332 shall conform to an average grain size of ASTM No. 5 or coarser.
7.3 Annealing Temperature — Alloy UNS N08330 shall be annealed at 1900°F (1040°C) minimum. Alloy UNS N08332 shall be annealed at 2100°F (1150°C) minimum.
8.1 All bars and shapes shall conform to the permissible variations in dimensions specified in Tables 3–14, inclusive.
9.1 The material shall be uniform in quality and temper, smooth, commercially straight, and free of injurious imperfections.
10.1.1 A lot for chemical analysis shall consist of one heat.

10.1.2 A lot for mechanical properties and grain size testing shall consist of material from one heat of the same condition and cross section, and in no case more than 30 000 lb (13 600 kg) in weight.
10.2.1 Chemical Analysis — Representative samples from each lot shall be taken during pouring or subsequent processing.
10.2.1.1 Product (check) analysis shall be wholly the responsibility of the purchaser.

10.2.2 Mechanical Properties and Grain Size — Samples of the material to provide test specimens for mechanical properties and grain size shall be taken from such locations in each lot as to be representative of that lot.
11.1 Chemical Analysis — One test per lot.
11.2 Grain Size — One test per lot.
11.3 Mechanical Properties — One test per lot.
12.1 Tension test specimens shall be taken from material in the final condition and tested in the direction of fabrication.

13.1 Chemical Composition — In case of dispute, the chemical analysis shall be made in accordance with Test Methods E 1473.

13.2 Grain Size — The measurement of average grain size may be carried out by the planimetric method, the comparison method, or the intercept method described in Test Methods E 112. In case of dispute the "referee" method for determining average grain size shall be the planimetric method.

14.1 Inspection of the material by the purchaser shall be as agreed upon between the purchaser and the supplier as part of the purchase contract.

15.1 Material that fails to conform to the requirements of this specification may be rejected. Rejection should be reported to the producer or supplier promptly and in writing. In case of dissatisfaction with the results of the test, the producer or supplier may make claim for a rehearing.

16.1 A producer's or supplier's certification shall be furnished to the purchaser that the material was manufactured, sampled, tested, and inspected in accordance with this specification and has been found to meet the requirements. A report of the test results shall be furnished.
17.1 Material shall be bundled or boxed in such a manner as to assure undamaged delivery to its destination when properly transported by a common carrier.
17.2 Each bundle or shipping container shall be marked with the name of the material or UNS number, heat number,
condition (temper), this specification number, the size, gross, and net weight, consignor and consignee address, and contract or order number.
